_comment: Phase 4. The egress limiter is shedding load, which means this system is at
the edge of a provider's contracted TPS and is refusing its own traffic to
stay inside it.
WHY layer='egress' SPECIFICALLY
RateLimitMetrics tags three layers and they are three different pages.
merchant means one caller is over their allowance - their problem, and the
system is working. endpoint means this service is at capacity - scale or
shed. egress means we are about to breach somebody else's contract, which
is the one with a commercial consequence and the only one worth waking
somebody for. Alerting on the untagged total would fire for a single noisy
merchant and read as an outage.
THIS ALERT IS WHY THE METERS CHANGED
increase over the window, not the raw total - 'saturating' is a rate, and a
cumulative total crossing a threshold once would latch the alert on forever
since counters do not come back down.
That query was impossible until phase 4e. These counters were registered
with Gauge.builder, so SigNoz typed them as gauges and its increase summed
raw samples instead of differencing them: 36 over a window in which the
value never left 4. Declaring the metric a Sum through the metadata API did
not help, because the query path reads the temporality label written on each
sample at ingest. The fix was FunctionCounter at the emitter.

annotations.description: The egress rate limiter refused calls in the last window. This system is at a provider's contracted TPS ceiling and is dropping its own traffic to avoid breaching it.
